books.title: The Software Architect Elevator: Redefining the Architect's Role
books.description: Defines architects as people who bridge the gap in large enterprises: they work with technical staff and convey technical topics to upper management, while translating business strategy into supporting technical decisions.

books.title: Software Architecture for Developers
books.description: A practical, pragmatic, and lightweight software architecture guide specifically aimed at software developers.

books.title: Software Architecture: The Hard Parts
books.description: A narrative about a team breaking down an old monolithic application into microservices, with practical trade-off analysis for refactoring a large monolith.

books.title: Just Enough Software Architecture
books.description: An approachable and comprehensive book on software architecture.

books.title: Software Systems Architecture
books.description: A practitioner-oriented guide to designing and implementing effective architectures for information systems.

books.title: Fundamentals of Software Architecture
books.description: Covers people skills, modularity, component-based thinking, and architectural styles.

books.title: Enterprise Integration Patterns
books.description: Guidance for connecting systems without coupling them too tightly.

books.title: Pattern-Oriented Software Architecture
books.description: One of the most comprehensive references for distributed system design.

books.title: Building Evolutionary Architectures
books.description: Explains how fitness functions can guide architectural change over time.

books.title: Domain-Driven Design
books.description: Promotes building a Ubiquitous Language that embeds domain terminology into software, with models defined and evolved over a product's life.

books.title: Thinking in Systems
books.description: A system is more than the sum of its parts and may exhibit adaptive, dynamic, goal-seeking, self-preserving, and evolutionary behavior.

books.title: Design Patterns
books.description: Design patterns help make balanced decisions on code design.

books.title: Clean Code
books.description: Good software starts with good code, emphasizing naming, single-purpose functions, and formatting.

books.title: Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code
books.description: A disciplined technique for restructuring existing code by altering its internal structure without changing external behavior.

books.title: Building Microservices (2nd Edition)
books.description: Architectural trade-offs and considerations in distributed system design.

books.title: Release It! (2nd Edition)
books.description: Architecture stability decisions and building 'cynical' software; stability patterns and foundational production knowledge.

books.title: Designing Data Intensive Systems
books.description: A mini-encyclopedia of modern data engineering: replication, partitioning, transactions, event logs, and more.

books.title: Don't make me think, revisited: a common sense approach to Web usability
books.description: A practical guide for understanding web usability and user experience.

books.title: System Design Interview (Volume 1 & 2)
books.description: Strengthen your systems design muscle for day-to-day architectural work, not just interview prep.

books.title: Accelerate
books.description: If you want to move faster, you need to accelerate—the second derivative of position.

books.title: The Phoenix Project (and The Unicorn Project)
books.description: A best-selling novel about DevOps; emphasizes security-first thinking and breaking down silos between development and operations.

books.title: Continuous Delivery
books.description: Through automation of build, deployment, and testing, and improved collaboration, teams can release changes in hours or minutes.
